submitted.rationale: Idx 12 (Al 0.39 / Sb 0.61) had the highest measured EQE, 0.00117 %, of the three measurements. Every value was close to zero, which points to a weakly active library at 2.1 eV illumination.

rejected.reason: EQE 0.00063 %, lower than idx 12, even though MEGNet predicted sub-2.1 eV gaps for Sb2O4 and Sb6O13 at this Sb-rich end.
EQE -0.0012 % (no photoresponse), even though MEGNet predicted a 1.04 eV gap for Al2Sb2O7.

consultations.verdict: Support. MEGNet HSE gaps: Sb2O4 1.67 eV and Sb6O13 2.05 eV are below the 2.1 eV photon energy. The Al-Sb ternaries AlSbO4 (3.65) and Al5Sb3O16 (3.74) and Sb2O3 (2.8) are not. Absorption at 2.1 eV therefore needs Sb-rich mixed-valence oxide, so the most Sb-rich end (idx 20) is the best first measurement.

Mixed. MACE puts AlSbO4 on the hull, so the region near 50:50 should form a stable rutile AlSbO4 plus an Sb-oxide matrix. On a pure-gap basis that is not favoured (3.65 eV). But the EQE at the Sb-rich end was very low (6e-4 %), so the gap argument alone is not predicting merit well. I'm probing mid-composition idx 12 (Sb 0.61) to sample a different phase region.

Support. MEGNet HSE gap for Al2Sb2O7 (Al:Sb 50:50) is 1.04 eV, well below 2.1 eV, so a 50:50 composition could absorb. Index 10 (Sb 0.49) also shows extra XRD peaks (Q 1.95, 2.53) that are absent at the Sb-rich end. EQE rose from idx 20 to idx 12, which fits the trend toward mid-composition.
